# UFC Fight Predictions

## KNN Model

This file is dedicated to making and evaluating a k nearest neighbors model to predict UFC fights.

### Preparation

```{r}
scaled_ufc_model <- readRDS("scaled_ufc_model.rds") # Read in dataset from MainUFCProject.Rmd (Main) file

# Split the dataset
ratio <- 0.7
set.seed(12345)
train_rows <- sample(1:nrow(scaled_ufc_model), ratio * nrow(scaled_ufc_model))
ufc_train_df <- scaled_ufc_model[train_rows, ]
ufc_test_df  <- scaled_ufc_model[-train_rows, ]
```

## Make KNN Model

```{r}
library(class)

knn_predict_winner <- knn(train = ufc_train_df[, -10], # Exclude Column 10, which is $Winner
                       test  = ufc_test_df[, -10],
                       cl    = ufc_train_df[, 10], # Column 10 is the dependent variable
                       k     = 11,
                       prob  = TRUE)
knn_predict_winner
```

Through trial and error, k is the number of nearest neighbors for which kappa is still positive while accuracy and sensitivity is relatively high (at least compared to other values of k).

## Evaluate KNN Model

```{r}
library(caret)
confusionMatrix(as.factor(ufc_predict_winner), as.factor(ufc_test_df$Winner), positive = "1")
saveRDS(knn_predict_winner, "knn_predict_winner.rds")
```

Kappa for the KNN model is 0.18, which is a little better at making predictions compared to chance. Sensitivity is just over 2/3, and accuracy is only 61%. Specificity is just above 1/2. Overall, this is nowhere near a satisfactory model, but it is a relatively well-rounded one for both general predicting and for prioritizing predicting positives accurately.
